identifications.note: This arc COUNTS the freedom in the crossing's only remaining target and performs no comparison; F2 is untouched and nothing is read. Its consequence for the row is a RECOMMENDATION NOT TO SPEND IT: R11's arithmetic (outputs - consumed anchors > 0, else vacuous by MB12) fails on either branch, because the mirror set is ONE row while the residual freedom is a 48-fold discrete selection (log2 48 ~ 5.58 bits) or, if the whole orbit is used, a 48-element target set. I-13's price is therefore now KNOWN and UNAFFORDABLE at present outputs, which is a sharper statement than 'unearned' -- the crossing is not blocked by missing effort but by an arithmetic that does not close.

claim_one_line: THE MIRROR SECTOR POSED: THE RESIDUAL FREEDOM IS 48, AND R11'S ARITHMETIC SAYS DO NOT SPEND THE LAST ROW. Of KIND_TABLE's four coupling rows, tones, probability and phases are all CONSUMED with decisive MISSes and the MIRROR SET (theta-even) is the last licensed row, delivered by B1011 C6 and never drawn on by any sealed comparison; the one-shot rule consumes CONTACT ROWS, so it is spent whatever the outcome. B1348 posed the theta-ODD plane, which is NOT the crossing target; this poses the right one. CONTROLS: the canonical rational basis from the weights (e(0,0), e(1,1), e(0,1)+e(1,0), e(0,2)+e(2,0)) satisfies C v = +v; <R,L> restricts exactly; the PROJECTIVE IMAGE IS 720 = 12 x 60 = A_4 x A_5, as forced since (-1,-1) and (-1,1) act as scalars on V_2 (x) V_2; C^4_even is IRREDUCIBLE; and a random direction has |Stab| = 1 with orbit 720. THE STABILISER SPECTRUM, every orbit size dividing 720 as orbit-stabiliser requires: |Stab| = 15, 10, 9, 6, 5, 3, 2 giving orbits 48, 72, 80, 120, 144, 240, 360. MAXIMAL |Stab| = 15, SO THE SMALLEST DISTINGUISHED ORBIT HAS 48 ELEMENTS -- four times the odd plane's 12. The structure is confirmed rather than assumed: 15 = 3 x 5 = (tetrahedral vertex stabiliser) x (icosahedral vertex stabiliser), and the maximal-stabiliser direction is RANK 1, singular values [1,0], a PRODUCT STATE v (x) w. METHOD CORRECTION recorded not hidden: a first pass orbit-decomposed by rounding projective coordinates and produced sizes that DO NOT DIVIDE 720 (68, 370, 423...), impossible by orbit-stabiliser; that enumeration is WITHDRAWN and the table is derived from stabiliser orders alone with |orbit| = 720/|Stab| -- the same float-drift failure as B1348's withdrawn step 4, caught by an invariant the answer must satisfy. R11'S ARITHMETIC, THE POINT OF THE ARC: on branch A (the row needs one direction) the anchor cost is a 48-FOLD DISCRETE SELECTION, log2 48 ~ 5.58 bits; on branch B (the row uses the whole orbit) there is no selection but the prediction becomes a 48-ELEMENT SET, a 48-fold look-elsewhere on the comparison side; and the mirror row is ONE row, so ON EITHER BRANCH OUTPUTS MINUS ANCHORS IS NEGATIVE AND R11 DECLARES THE CELL VACUOUS BEFORE THE SEAL. RECOMMENDATION, STATED AS A RESULT: DO NOT SPEND THE LAST ROW -- not now, and on this arithmetic not through this row at all, unless the mirror set's value set is shown to carry MORE THAN ONE independent output, in which case the outputs are recounted and R11 re-evaluated. Three of four rows are spent with decisive misses and the fourth is unrepeatable, so a gating computation that says NO is worth more than a fourth miss and costs less. WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: count the mirror set's independent outputs (k > 5.6 bits closes the ledger); cut the 48 (the Galois question at the point level is OPEN, B1348's withdrawal having left it so); or add a new licensed row under R5 in advance, derived not fitted since F1 forbids fitting. FENCES: F2 untouched, no comparison performed, no value read, I-13 still UNEARNED, R4/R5/R10 left as banked. The exactification debt B1348 registered applies to both arcs. NUMBERING: this takes B1349, the last id before the reserved range B1350-B1399 (E71); the next new arc on this branch needs a range grant. ADDENDUM (same branch, NOT a new arc -- B1350-B1399 is reserved, so the work discharging B1349's own debt is banked here). (1) THE EXACTIFICATION OWED BY B1348 AND B1349 IS PAID: the instrument is rebuilt in exact Q(zeta_60) = Q[z]/Phi_60, every exponent landing in (1/15)Z so every entry is a Z-combination of zeta_60 powers (T = diag(z15^-2, z15^2, z15^8, z15^2, z15^7, z15^8); S = -i/(5 sqrt3) sum_w sgn(w) z15^{-3<w(l+rho),m+rho>} with i = zeta_60^15 and sqrt3 = zeta_60^5 + zeta_60^-5), and every control passes with NO FLOAT ANYWHERE: S Sdag = I, S = S^T, C = S^2 has entries in {0,1} and IS the charge conjugation (a,b) -> (b,a), and (ST)^3 = S^2. The integers both arcs' verdicts rest on are unchanged. (2) GALOIS DOES CUT, AND MEASURABLY: a direction with RATIONAL coordinates in the weight basis is fixed by every sigma in Gal(Q(zeta_60)/Q) automatically, so the question becomes how many distinguished directions are rational -- and that number, not the orbit size, is what R7 prices. theta-ODD: 12 -> 2 RATIONAL ([1:0] and [0:1], i.e. f1 and f2), cost log2 2 = 1 bit. theta-EVEN (the crossing target): 8 RATIONAL of the 96 maximal-stabiliser directions, cost log2 8 = 3 BITS, down from 5.58. The eight are the four canonical weight basis vectors plus four more with entries in {0, 1, -1/2}. STRUCTURE: the 96 are TWO orbits of 48, forced because A_4 has TWO classes of stabiliser-3 points (vertices and faces, four each), 2 x (4 x 12) = 96; the 4/4 split of the rationals between them is INDICATED, NOT ESTABLISHED. (3) R11 RECOMPUTED: anchor cost falls from 5.58 bits to 3 bits while outputs stay at 1, so outputs - anchors moves from -4.6 to -2. STILL SHORT, BUT THE RECOMMENDATION CHANGES SHAPE -- from 'not through this row at all' to 'ONE MORE OUTPUT THAN THREE AND IT CLOSES': if the mirror set's exact value set carries at least 4 independent numbers the ledger balances and the arc becomes worth its one shot. That is a concrete checkable follow-up where before there was none. (4) TWO ERRORS CAUGHT AND RECORDED: the rationality test first ACCEPTED 1/phi, because with tol 1e-8 and denominators to 10^4 the Fibonacci ratio 4181/6765 approximates it to ~1e-8 -- in an instrument whose value set is the golden nine that is the worst possible false positive; fixed to tol 1e-11 and denominators to 1000, WITH A CONTROL asserting the test rejects 1/phi and accepts -1/2, and the reported 14 became 8. And the orbit enumeration drifted a THIRD time, reporting sizes [48, 68] with 68 not dividing 720; the 48 and the two-orbit structure rest on orbit-stabiliser and on A_4's two stabiliser-3 classes, and the enumeration is used for no banked number. (5) THE RECOMMENDATION NOW: still do not spend the row yet, but the reason has moved from structural to arithmetic by a measurable margin, and the next step is no longer 'cut the 48' -- that is done, 48 -> 8 -- it is COUNT HOW MANY INDEPENDENT NUMBERS THE theta-EVEN MIRROR SET CARRIES. Four suffices. ADDENDUM 2 (same branch, same id -- B1350-B1399 reserved): THE OUTPUTS ARE COUNTED AND THE ROW SPLITS IN TWO. THE LAW: on the theta-EVEN sector Re h is EAR-INDEPENDENT exactly when gcd(m,15) > 1, ear-DEPENDENT exactly on the 8 UNITS of Z/15 (phi(15) = 8); the verification is COMPLETE not inductive, since ord(R) = ord(L) = 15 so m = 1..15 is the entire family, and there are ZERO violations. Reading: the listener's direction matters precisely when R^m L^m still generates the full cyclic group. THE CRITERION IS ALGEBRAIC NOT STATISTICAL -- for a real ear v = Bc, Re h = c^T Sym(Re A) c / (c^T G c) with A = B^T (C R^m L^m) B, so ear-independence is the exact identity Sym(Re A) = lambda G, decided in Q(zeta_60) with no sampling and no tolerance; this retires the float-drift class that bit B1348 step 4 and B1349 twice. B856 IS REPRODUCED FROM AN INSTRUMENT SHARING NO CODE WITH IT AND STRENGTHENED: h(5) = -1 exactly, |h|^2 in {1/(phi sqrt5), phi/sqrt5, 1} with the golden pair summing to 1, Re h(1) = 1/(2phi); B856 reports ear-independence at m=1 numerically (2e-16) and here it is an EXACT identity for every m = 1..15; h_odd(5) = -1 with C = -1 on odd means R^5 L^5|odd = +I, which IS B856's period-5 collapse, and m=15 on the even side gives lambda = 1 exactly since weld(15) = C = +1 there. EXACT EXTRA: tr(G^-1 Q_m) = 0 for ALL 8 units, so the ear-dependent readings are TRACELESS -- no mean, only spread. THE FIELD STRUCTURE: the four ear-independent values {-1/(2phi), 0, 1/2, 1} all lie in Q(sqrt5) inside Q(zeta_60), the field of the modular data itself, while EVERY ear-dependent eigenvalue is (1/(2 sqrt2)) x a unit of Z[phi] -- (1/(2sqrt2)){+-phi^2, +-1/phi} at m in {1,4,11,14} and (1/(2sqrt2)){+-sqrt5, +-1} at m in {2,7,8,13}, all eight PROVED from exact characteristic polynomials (radsimp(got-claim) = 0), never float-matched, because the b1349c trap had tol 1e-8 accept 4181/6765 as 1/phi. And sqrt2 IS NOT IN Q(zeta_60), proved twice: Phi_60 stays irreducible over Q(sqrt2) (factor degrees [16], compositum degree 32 != 16) and by Kronecker-Weber the conductor of Q(sqrt2) is 8, which does not divide 60; POSITIVE CONTROL, Phi_60 over Q(sqrt5) and over Q(-1/(2phi)) factors as [8,8] so those ARE inside. SELECTING AN EAR THEREFORE COSTS A FIELD EXTENSION THE MODULAR DATA DOES NOT CONTAIN -- addendum 1's Galois cut restated on the value side. THE COUNT, over R: dim_R span{Q_m} in Sym_4(R) is 3 over the whole period, 2 on the units, 1 on the non-units (all proportional to G); G lies in the span of all 15 but not of the units; either way there are 2 EAR-DISCRIMINATING DIRECTIONS. R11: BRANCH A (gcd(m,15) > 1, 7 words) consumes NO ear-anchor because no direction is selected, and yields 4 forced values, so outputs - anchors = +4, or +1 counting only -1/(2phi) (the lone value outside Q), or +1 even if ear-independence is ruled NOT to discharge the anchor -- IT CLOSES ON THREE OF FOUR READINGS, failing only if the conservative count and the undischarged anchor are combined. BRANCH B (gcd(m,15) = 1, 8 words) gives 2 outputs against 3 bits = -1 and DOES NOT CLOSE. THE FIRST POSITIVE INSTRUCTION THIS ARC HAS PRODUCED: if the row is ever spent, spend it on a word with gcd(m,15) > 1, where no ear is selected at all. THREE ERRORS RECORDED, NONE HIDDEN. (1) b1349d IS WITHDRAWN AS AN INSTRUMENT: it used R^m L^m unwelded and compared COMPLEX h across ears, where B856/B641 grade C R^m L^m and Re h over REAL ears. WHICH deviation mattered was MEASURED not assumed: dropping C only NEGATES lambda and Re h stays scalar, so the actual bug was complex-vs-real -- at m=1 on the odd sector spread|h| = 8.5e-01 while spread Re h = 1.1e-16. The missing C did one visible thing, flipping h(5) from -1 to +1. The control did its job: it refused to let the even number be read. E58 applied to my OWN paraphrase, not only to a relay. (2) THE PRE-REGISTRATION'S DECISION RULE WAS MIS-DERIVED: b1349d pre-registered 'ear-independent => outputs 0, R11 can NEVER close', importing AC4's bench demotion into R11, which prices CONSUMED anchors -- if the reading is direction-blind no direction is selected and the anchor is not consumed, so ear-independence HELPS the ledger. Backwards, and recorded rather than silently reversed. (3) A COUNTING ERROR OF MY OWN, caught by the test written against this addendum: a first pass reported dim span = 6 by taking the rank OVER Q of power-basis coefficient vectors, which measures Q-independence of field elements and inflates by the field degree; the honest quantity is dim_R span{Q_m} = 3, and the correction REVERSES branch B from +2 to -1. The 6 is withdrawn from both the findings and the script. A first draft also claimed the closure did not depend on the disputed anchor reading; that rested on the withdrawn 6 and is retracted. WHAT THIS DOES NOT LICENSE: R11 is an INPUT-ACCOUNTING gate, not a physics gate -- closing it says the cell is not vacuous under MB12 and says nothing about whether the row is right. B856 is the precedent ON THIS VERY QUANTITY: its |h|^2 reading was REFUTED ON KIND and the surviving Re h = 1/(2phi) sat in a 1-sigma window holding at least 17 natural candidates. Branch A's cheapest output is -1/(2phi), whose modulus is exactly the number the programme already failed to cash -- the honest reason not to read this as good news about physics. FENCES: F2 untouched, no comparison performed, no value read, nothing reaches CLAIMS.md, Gate 5 untouched, I-13 still UNEARNED (its price now known and affordable on one branch of two), verdict stays NEGATIVE. WHAT NOW GATES THE ROW IS KIND-CORRECTNESS, NOT ARITHMETIC. DUPLICATE CHECK RUN BEFORE CALLING THE LAW NEW (already_banked.py, two queries): no prior arc banks it; top hits are B1349 itself and B1011, the INPUT, already in depends_on. NEIGHBOURHOOD NOT DUPLICATION: B996 and B997 compute over the SAME words R^m L^m and also discriminate within that family by a number-theoretic condition on m, but neither mentions 15, gcd or coprimality (checked, not assumed) and their modulus is the SL(2,Z/N) shadow's conductor while this one is 15 = ord(R) = ord(L) in the SU(3)_2 modular data. Three arcs now cut the metallic family by arithmetic in m; whether the cuts are related is OPEN and not investigated here. ADDENDUM 3: THE 4/4 SPLIT IS ESTABLISHED AND BRANCH B TIES AT ZERO. Addendum 1 left the split of the 8 rational directions between the two orbits of 48 explicitly INDICATED NOT ESTABLISHED; it is now exact. Computed in Q(zeta_60) with projective canonicalisation by exact field inversion, so two directions compare equal iff they ARE equal, and with |orbit| divides 720 ASSERTED for all eight -- the invariant that caught three earlier float drifts (68, 370, 423). ORBIT 1 (size 48, |Stab| 15): e1, e2, (1,0,0,1), (0,1,1,0). ORBIT 2 (size 48, |Stab| 15): e3, e4, (1,0,0,-1/2), (0,1,-1/2,0). SPLIT = [4,4] over exactly two orbits. Control run first: R and L restrict to the theta-even sector EXACTLY (M6.Bev = Bev.M4, symbolic), so the 4x4 action is the 6x6 one. This also upgrades addendum 1's two-orbit structure from ARGUED (A_4's two stabiliser-3 classes) to VERIFIED by direct exact enumeration; scope, what is established is that the EIGHT RATIONALS occupy exactly two orbits of 48 four each, while the whole maximal-stabiliser set being 96 = 2 x 48 still rests on addendum 1's A_4 argument. THE CONSEQUENCE: confined to ONE orbit -- which it is whenever the orbit is GENERATED from a starting point rather than chosen -- the anchor is log2(4) = 2 BITS, not 3. So BRANCH B READS 2 - 2 = 0 AND FAILS BY A TIE, R11 requiring strictly > 0: a sharper negative than addendum 2's -1. One more ear-discriminating direction would close it AND THERE IS PROVABLY NO THIRD, since dim_R span{Q_m : m a unit} = 2 exactly. Branch B does not fail for want of effort; it fails by one dimension the sector does not contain. Branch A now closes on four of six readings instead of three of four, the two failures being the same combination as before (conservative output count TOGETHER WITH ruling that ear-independence does not discharge the anchor). Verdict stays NEGATIVE, I-13 stays UNEARNED, and addendum 2's closing judgement stands verbatim: WHAT GATES THE ROW NOW IS KIND-CORRECTNESS, NOT ARITHMETIC.
